Flag outliers using the methods of move2utils

Source: R/event_flag_outliers.R
event_flag_outliers.Rd

This function detects outlying locations with one of the methods of the package move2utils, which requires the suggested package move2utils (install it with remotes::install_github("move2universe/move2utils")). Most methods choose their thresholds from the data, so, unlike event_flag_mcconnell(), they do not require a maximum speed.

Usage

event_flag_outliers(
  x,
  method = c("clean_track", "speed_cap", "detour", "bridge", "probability"),
  ...
)

Arguments

x

A move2 object.

method

The method used to detect outliers, one of "clean_track" (the default), "speed_cap", "detour", "bridge" or "probability" (see Details).

...

Further arguments passed to the move2utils function of the chosen method.

Value

A logical vector of the same length as the number of events in x, indicating which events are valid (TRUE) and which are outliers (FALSE).

Details

The available methods are:

  • "clean_track" (the default): move2utils::mt_clean_track(), which combines the methods below and iterates until no more outliers are found; it is the recommended starting point.

  • "speed_cap": move2utils::mt_flag_speed_cap(), which flags events on either side of an implausibly fast step, with a cap chosen from the data or given as v_max (with threshold_type = "hard").

  • "detour": move2utils::mt_flag_outliers_detour(), which flags events for which the path to and from the neighbouring events is much longer than the direct distance between them (e.g. out-and-back spikes).

  • "bridge": move2utils::mt_flag_outliers_bridge(), which flags events that are far from where a Brownian bridge between the neighbouring events would put them.

  • "probability": move2utils::mt_flag_outliers(), which flags events with an improbable combination of speed, turning angle and their changes.

Further arguments are passed to the move2utils function through ... (see its documentation for the options). Physical quantities must be given as units objects (e.g. v_max = as_units(50, "km/h")), and are converted to the units expected by move2utils: speeds (v_max, physiological_ceiling), distances (location_error, jitter, residual_floor, step_floor, min_leg) and masses (mass). location_error (for the "clean_track" and "bridge" methods) can be a single value, one value per event, the name of a column of x with the errors (as a units object), or "auto", with which move2utils uses the column eobs_horizontal_accuracy_estimate (which must then be a units object) or, failing that, the Argos location classes. state (for the "clean_track" method) can be the name of a column of x, or one value per event. Each track is checked on its own, with all the arguments (unless pool_by pools thresholds across tracks). The move2utils functions are run without plots and messages; to inspect their diagnostics, call them directly on x.

x must be ordered by time within each track (see tt_order_time()). Some methods also require events with duplicated times to be removed first (e.g. with move2::mt_filter_unique()). Events without a location are ignored, and returned as valid. Tracks with too few events with a location for the method (10 for "clean_track", 5 for "probability", and 2 for the other methods) are not checked, with a warning, and their events are returned as valid.

See also

tt_clean_outliers() to remove the outliers, or replace their location.

Examples

event_flag_outliers(example_tt, method = "detour")
#>  [1] TRUE TRUE TRUE TRUE TRUE TRUE TRUE TRUE TRUE TRUE TRUE TRUE TRUE TRUE TRUE
# use a maximum speed rather than one estimated from the data (steps in
# this toy dataset are hundreds of km long)
event_flag_outliers(
  example_tt,
  method = "speed_cap",
  v_max = as_units(1000, "km/h"),
  threshold_type = "hard"
)
#>  [1] FALSE FALSE  TRUE FALSE FALSE  TRUE  TRUE FALSE FALSE  TRUE FALSE FALSE
#> [13]  TRUE FALSE FALSE
